_comment: SENTINEL (index >= 90, excluded from the coverage metric by design): this is an ENVIRONMENT probe, not a pitfall fixture -- it reads the install feature flags out of deal.II's config.h and reports which of the catalog's assumed features (MPI, p4est, PETSc, Trilinos, SLEPc) this build actually has. It was previously keyed adaptive_refinement::0, a physics that does not exist in the deal.II registry, so it credited no claim while looking like coverage; rekeyed to the sentinel range on 2026-08-06 so that it plainly credits none. It is the evidence behind the 'parallel_poisson cannot be verified on this host' finding: MPI, P4EST, PETSC, TRILINOS and SLEPC are all undefined in this install. Tier-2 for dealii adaptive_refinement#: probe install feature flags from config.h to expose the gap between catalog claims (p4est, MPI, PETSc, Trilinos, SLEPc) and what the current conda-forge dealii-9.1.1 install actually has compiled. The 9.1.1 default has all parallelism features UNDEFINED — a serial-only build. This fixture PASSES whenever it can detect ANY dealii install and produce a feature report; it fails only when config.h is missing entirely. Output 'catalog_claims_install_doesnt_support' is the falsification ledger for the current install state — when task #30 (deal.II rebuild) lands, the same fixture will record an empty ledger. Verified empirically 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — the hook is left in source.py, no recipe is declared, because a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding. T2_MUTATE=1 points the same probe at the OTHER deal.II on this host, whose flags are the mirror image of the one normally found, and the fixture STILL PASSES. Measured 2026-08-07: unmutated it read /usr/include/deal.II/base/config.h (dealii_version=9.1.1) and reported features_on=[HDF5, LAPACK, MPI, MUPARSER, P4EST, PETSC, SLEPC, TRILINOS], features_off=[METIS], catalog_claims_install_doesnt_support=[]; mutated it read ~/dealii/build/include/deal.II/base/config.h (dealii_version=9.8.0) and reported features_off=[HDF5, MPI, P4EST, PETSC, SLEPC, TRILINOS] and FIVE broken catalog claims. Same fixture, opposite report, both green. That is structural: every expect_in_output string is a bare `key=` prefix that main() prints unconditionally, so the only thing this fixture asserts is that SOME config.h was found — never what it says. Two consequences worth reading twice. First, the sentence above, 'MPI, P4EST, PETSC, TRILINOS and SLEPC are all undefined in this install', is FALSE for the install this fixture actually reads on this host, and the fixture passes anyway. Second, an expectation naming a measured value (e.g. a specific features_off entry) would make it discriminate; that change is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a control stops being evidence. Re-run by hand: `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/Schreibtisch/open-fem-agent/.venv/bin/python source.py`.
